name: China Masters
stakes: This Super 750 event offers a vital opportunity for India's top shuttlers to consolidate their rankings and build momentum after the World Championships, especially for those looking to rebound from recent setbacks.
summary:
The China Masters, a Super 750 event, is set to kick off in Shenzhen, and India's contingent is geared up for another challenging week on the BWF tour. While the draw is yet to be announced, anticipation is high for how India's top shuttlers will fare. Men's Doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fifth and ranked fifth globally, lead the charge, looking to build on their World Championships quarterfinal run despite lingering fitness concerns. Their performance will be crucial for India's medal hopes.

Women's Doubles duo Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand are riding a wave of confidence after their historic bronze medal at the World Championships, and all eyes will be on them to see if they can maintain their red-hot form. In singles, PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen, both ranked in the top 15, will be eager to rebound after relatively early exits at the Worlds. Veteran HS Prannoy and the rising Mixed Doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also feature in a strong Indian lineup, each aiming to make a deep run and secure valuable ranking points.
